sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused Nos.2 and 4 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing FIR in Crime No.162/2022 registered by Kodigehalli police on the private complaint preferred by respondent No.2 under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 471, 468, 120B, 34 of IPC.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The case of prosecution/complainant before the Magistrate is that accused No.5 introduced accused No.1 to her husband and accused No.1 said to be purchased site No.6A from the complainant on 20.11.2019.

Subsequently, accused No.1 said to be informed the complainant that she was required for rectification of the sale deed and they took her to Sub- Registrar office and by fraudulent manner, got registered two sites one on 13.12.2019 in respect of site No.5A and another site No.5 on 16.12.2019.
Though accused No.1 is the friend of complainant's husband and undertaken to pay money, not paid money.
Though the payment of sale consideration was shown in the sale deed, but actually no money was transferred to the complainant towards sale consideration.

sentences.text: Therefore, the complainant filed first information to the police, but they did not register FIR and the complainant approached the higher officer DCP, who has also not registered FIR.
Therefore, a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. was filed and it NC: 2024:KHC:2362 was got referred to the police and in turn, the police registered FIR, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that actually, accused No.2 purchased site from the complainant by paying the sale consideration.
Both the sale deeds were executed by the complainant in the Sub-Registrar Office and her son also accompanied her to the Sub-Registrar Office.
They received cash and executed the sale deed in favour of accused No.2 and purposefully cheated accused persons.
It is further contended that the complainant filed civil suit against accused No.1 for cancellation of sale deed, which is pending before the Civil Court.
The dispute is civil in nature.
Even otherwise, the police have investigated the matter and filed 'B' report as against accused Nos.1, 3 and 5.
Therefore, there is no ingredient to attract Section 420 of IPC, when the dispute is purely civil in nature.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- complainant objected the petition and contended that the petitioners took the complainant in the name of rectification of sale deed which was executed by the complainant in favour of NC: 2024:KHC:2362 accused No.1, but they did not pay money.

They got registered the sale deed and since accused No.1 was the friend of complainant's husband, she did not force him to pay the money immediately, but accused No.1 undertook to pay the money and not paid, and cheated the complainant.
Therefore, the complaint has been filed before the police which has not been entertained.
Thereafter, the private complaint has been filed.
The police have not at all investigated the matter.
No notice has been issued in favour of respondent.
Therefore, filed protest petition before the Magistrate challenging the B-final report, which is pending consideration.
Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for dismissing the petition.
6. The learned High Court Government Pleader objected the petition and contended that the investigation officer issued notice to complainant, but she has not cooperated with investigation officer.

Therefore, the B-final report has been filed against accused Nos.1 and 5.
7.
Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, perused the records.
It is an admitted fact that the complainant being the landlord, formulated layout after obtaining conversion order from the Government and sold to various persons.
She said to be sold site No.6A to accused No.1 on 20.11.2019.

Subsequently, it is alleged that at the instance of accused No.1, for the purpose of rectification of the said sale deed, she went to the Sub-Registrar Office, but, accused No.1 in collusion with others, got registered sale deed in favour of accused No.2 and without paying money, the sale deed has been executed.

No money has been paid to the complainant and therefore,
it is contended that she has filed suit through her husband, the GPA holder, for cancelling the sale deed.

sentences.text: On perusal of the rival contention of the parties, especially, the complainant is said to be executed sale deed in favour of accused No.1 on 20.11.2019.
It is not in dispute that accused No.1 has already sold site to accused No.3 against whom the police have filed the B-final report.

If the contention of respondent No.2-complainant that she was taken to the Sub- Registrar Office for rectification of sale deed is accepted, the question of signing the document twice on 13.12.2019 for executing the sale deed in favour of accused No.2 in respect of NC: 2024:KHC:2362 site No.5A and once again, going to Sub-Registrar Office and executing the sale deed on 16.12.2019 in respect of site number No.5,
does not arise.

If at all the petitioners-accused tried to cheat or misrepresented the complainant and fraudulently obtained signature, the question of going to Sub- Registrar Office twice for executing the sale deed does not arise.

That apart, the complainant has also stated that she has not received sale consideration from accused No.1 and the petitioner-accused No.2.
10.

The complainant can agitate that without consideration, the sale is void and also can content that the sale deed is not at all the sale deed in the eye of law, if able to prove his case in civil side.
The complainant has filed a suit through her son and husband against the present petitioner and the accused No.1 and against other persons for cancellation of sale deed.
The Civil Court has already seized the matter in respect of executing the sale deed without payment and the Civil Court will take care of the complainant in the civil suit.
The police have already verified the document in the Sub-Registrar Office and thereafter, filed the B-final report.

Though the B-final report is challenged,
it is not against the NC: 2024:KHC:2362 petitioner.
Therefore, this Court cannot give finding on the B- final report.
Looking to the facts of the case, the dispute purely civil in nature.
The complainant's son, who is an educated person, went to the Sub-Registrar Office.
The respondent No.2- complainant is said to be uneducated, but she has filed signed in the Vakalath, which reveals that she cannot be uneducated.
Such being the case, the question of conducting investigation or filing charge sheet, does not arise.
Apart from that, the police have already investigated the case and filed 'B' final report as against the other accused persons.
Such being the case, the petitioners have made out a case for quashing FIR.
11. Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed.

The FIR in crime No.162/2022 registered against accused Nos.2 and 4 by the Kodigehalli Police and PCR No.11366/2022 dated 30.06.2022 filed before the VII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bangalore, are here by quashed.
